title.zh: 第七 祭祀上 光武即位告天 郊 封禪
title.en: Volume 97: Rituals and Worship Part One
title.raw: 第七 祭祀上 光武即位告天 郊 封禪 Volume 97: Rituals and Worship Part One

sentences.zh: 志第七 祭祀上

translations.literal: Treatise Seven: Sacrifices, Part One.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 7: Sacrifices, Part One.

sentences.zh: 光武即位告天 郊 封禅

translations.literal: Guangwu’s accession: announcement to Heaven; suburban sacrifice; feng and shan.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu’s accession: reporting to Heaven, the suburban rites, and the feng and shan sacrifices on Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 祭祀之道，自生民以來則有之矣。

translations.literal: As for the way of sacrifice, from the time the people first arose there have been such things.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of sacrifice has existed ever since human society began.

sentences.zh: 豺獺知祭祀，而況人乎！

translations.literal: Jackals and otters know sacrifice; how much more so human beings!
translations.idiomatic: Even jackals and otters observe sacrificial customs; surely people can do no less.

sentences.zh: 故人知之至於念想，猶豺獺之自然也，顧古質略而後文飾耳。

translations.literal: Therefore for people to know it reaching to thoughts and recollections is like the naturalness of jackals and otters; only that antiquity was plain and simple and later times added ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Human beings carry sacrifice in mind and memory as instinctively as those beasts do in nature; the difference is simply that early ages kept the rites spare and later ages elaborated them.

sentences.zh: 自古以來王公所爲羣祀，至於王莽，《漢書·郊祀志》既著矣，故今但列自中興以來所修用者，以爲《祭祀志》。

translations.literal: From antiquity the mass sacrifices performed by kings and dukes down to Wang Mang are already set forth in the “Treatise on Suburban Sacrifice” in the Hanshu; therefore here only those instituted and used since the restoration are listed, to form the “Treatise on Sacrifice.”
translations.idiomatic: The great state sacrifices of kings and nobles down through Wang Mang are already recorded in the Book of Han’s “Suburban Sacrifices”; this treatise therefore confines itself to what has been established and practiced since the dynasty’s revival.

sentences.zh: 建武元年，光武即位于鄗，爲壇營於鄗之陽。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwu, Guangwu took the throne at Hao and built an altar enclosure on the south side of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu 1 (25 CE), Guangwu was enthroned at Hao, where he raised an altar on the sunny slope south of the town.

sentences.zh: 祭告天地，采用元始中郊祭故事。

translations.literal: He sacrificed and announced to Heaven and Earth, adopting the precedent of the suburban sacrifices in the Yuanshi era.
translations.idiomatic: He reported his accession to Heaven and Earth, following the suburban-sacrifice precedents of the Yuanshi period (1–5 CE).

sentences.zh: 六宗羣神皆從，未以祖配。

translations.literal: The Six Ancestors and the host of spirits all attended; he had not yet matched the Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Honored Powers and the full pantheon were included, but no imperial ancestor was yet paired at the high altar.

sentences.zh: 天地共犢，餘牲尚約。

translations.literal: Heaven and Earth shared one calf; the remaining victims still tended toward simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth received a single calf between them; other offerings were still kept comparatively modest.

sentences.zh: 其文曰：「皇天上帝，后土神祇，睠顧降命，屬秀黎元，爲民父母，秀不敢當。

translations.literal: The text said: “August Heaven, Supreme Lord; Sovereign Earth, numinous powers—you have turned your gaze and sent down the charge, entrusting Xiu to the black-haired people as father and mother to the folk; Xiu does not dare accept this.”
translations.idiomatic: The prayer read: “August Heaven and High God, Sovereign Earth and the spirits—you have looked down and issued your mandate, setting Xiu over the common people as their parent; Xiu dares not presume to accept such a burden.”

sentences.zh: 羣下百僚，不謀同辭。

translations.literal: The host of officials below, without prior counsel, spoke with one voice.
translations.idiomatic: Every minister below, without having plotted together beforehand, spoke as one.

sentences.zh: 咸曰王莽篡弑竊位，秀發憤興義兵，破王邑百萬眾於昆陽，誅王郎、銅馬、赤眉、青犢賊，平定天下，海内蒙恩，上當天心，下爲元元所歸。

translations.literal: They all said: Wang Mang usurped and murdered and stole the throne; Xiu, stirred by indignation, raised righteous troops, broke Wang Yi’s million men at Kunyang, executed Wang Lang and the Bronze Horse, Red Eyebrows, and Green Calf bandits, pacified all under Heaven, and within the seas the people received grace; above he matches Heaven’s mind, below he is what the common folk turn to.
translations.idiomatic: They declared that Wang Mang had seized the throne by murder and usurpation; that Xiu, roused to action, had raised a loyal army, shattered Wang Yi’s host of a million at Kunyang, put down Wang Lang and the Bronze Horse, Red Eyebrows, and Green Calf rebels, restored peace to the realm, and won the gratitude of every shore—that Heaven above approved him and the people below rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 讖記曰：『劉秀發兵捕不道，卯金修德爲天子。

translations.literal: A prophecy text said: “Liu Xiu raises troops to seize the lawless; the metal of Mao cultivates virtue and becomes Son of Heaven.”
translations.idiomatic: The apocrypha ran: “Liu Xiu takes up arms against the wicked; the Liu house, refining its virtue, is destined for the throne.”

sentences.zh: 』秀猶固辭，至於再，至於三。

translations.literal: ” Xiu still firmly declined, to a second time, to a third time.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yet Xiu still refused—once, twice, and yet again.

sentences.zh: 羣下曰：『皇天大命，不可稽留。

translations.literal: The host below said: “The great charge of August Heaven cannot be delayed.
translations.idiomatic: His officers replied: “Heaven’s great mandate brooks no delay.”

sentences.zh: 』敢不敬承！」

translations.literal: ” How dare we not respectfully receive it!”
translations.idiomatic: ” How could we fail to accept it with reverence!”

sentences.zh: 二年正月，初制郊兆於于雒陽城南七里，依鄗。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, he first laid out the suburban-sacrifice precinct seven li south of Luoyang city, modeled on Hao.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jianwu 2 (26 CE), he first marked out the suburban altar seven li south of Luoyang, following the layout used at Hao.

sentences.zh: 采元始中故事。

translations.literal: He adopted the precedents of the Yuanshi era.
translations.idiomatic: The design drew on the Yuanshi-era precedents.

sentences.zh: 爲圓壇八陛，中又爲重壇，天地位其上，皆南嚮乡，西上。

translations.literal: They made a round mound with eight stairways; inside it they made a double mound; Heaven and Earth had their positions on it; all faced south; ascending was from the west.
translations.idiomatic: They built a round altar with eight flights of steps and a nested inner terrace; Heaven and Earth were set atop it, every station facing south, with approach from the west.

sentences.zh: 其外壇上爲五帝位。

translations.literal: On its outer mound were made the positions of the Five Thearchs.
translations.idiomatic: The outer ring held the stations of the Five Thearchs.

sentences.zh: 青帝位在甲寅之地，赤帝位在丙巳之地，黄帝位在丁未之地，白帝位在庚申之地，黑帝位在壬亥之地。

translations.literal: The Green Thearch’s position was in the jiayin place; the Red Thearch’s in the bingsi; the Yellow Thearch’s in the dingwei; the White Thearch’s in the gengshen; the Black Thearch’s in the renhai.
translations.idiomatic: The Green Thearch stood at the jiayin compass point, the Red at bingsi, the Yellow at dingwei, the White at gengshen, and the Black at renhai.

sentences.zh: 其外壝，重營皆紫，以像紫宫；

translations.literal: Outside its enclosing wall, the layered enclosures were all purple, to resemble the Purple Palace;
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the inner wall the layered enclosures were draped in purple, evoking the Purple Palace constellation;

sentences.zh: 有四通道以爲門。

translations.literal: There were four thoroughfares serving as gates.
translations.idiomatic: Four avenues served as gates.

sentences.zh: 日月在中營内南道，日在東，月在西，北斗在北道之西，皆别位，不在羣神列中。

translations.literal: Sun and Moon were inside the inner enclosure on the south path; the Sun in the east, the Moon in the west; the Northern Dipper was west of the north path; all had separate positions and were not in the array of the host of spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Within the inner camp’s southern aisle stood the Sun and Moon—the Sun to the east, the Moon to the west—with the Northern Dipper west of the northern aisle; each had its own station apart from the general ranks of deities.

sentences.zh: 八陛，陛五十八醊，合四百六十四醊。

translations.literal: Eight stairways; each stairway fifty-eight zhui; in all four hundred sixty-four zhui.
translations.idiomatic: The eight flights of steps held fifty-eight ritual mounds apiece, four hundred sixty-four in all.

sentences.zh: 五帝陛郭，帝七十二醊，合三百六十五醊。

translations.literal: For the Five Thearchs’ stairway enclosures, each Thearch had seventy-two zhui; in all three hundred sixty-five zhui.
translations.idiomatic: Around the Five Thearchs’ steps ran seventy-two mounds for each ruler—three hundred sixty-five altogether, one for each day of the year.

sentences.zh: 中營四門，門五十四神，合二百一十六神。

translations.literal: The inner enclosure had four gates; each gate fifty-four spirits; in all two hundred sixteen spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The inner precinct’s four gates held fifty-four deities each—two hundred sixteen in total.

sentences.zh: 外營四門，門百八神，合四百三十二神。

translations.literal: The outer enclosure had four gates; each gate one hundred eight spirits; in all four hundred thirty-two spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The outer ring’s four gates held a hundred eight spirits apiece, four hundred thirty-two altogether.

sentences.zh: 皆背營内乡。

translations.literal: All turned their backs toward the inside of the enclosure and faced outward.
translations.idiomatic: Each deity faced outward, backs turned toward the center of the camp.

sentences.zh: 中營四門，門封神四，外營四門，門封神四，合三十二神。

translations.literal: The inner enclosure’s four gates, each gate enfeoffing four spirits; the outer enclosure’s four gates, each gate enfeoffing four spirits; in all thirty-two spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Four gate-gods were posted at each of the inner camp’s four doors and four at each outer door—thirty-two gate spirits in all.

sentences.zh: 凡千五百一十四神。

translations.literal: In all one thousand five hundred fourteen spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The pantheon numbered one thousand five hundred fourteen deities.

sentences.zh: 營即壝也。

translations.literal: The ying is the wei.
translations.idiomatic: Here “enclosure” (ying) means the earthen wall (wei) around the altar.

sentences.zh: 封，封土筑也。

translations.literal: Feng: piling earth and building.
translations.idiomatic: A feng is a mound of heaped earth.

sentences.zh: 背中營神，五星也，及中官宿五官神及五岳之屬也。

translations.literal: The spirits with their backs to the inner enclosure are the Five Planets, and the spirits of the Central Palace lodges and the Five Offices, and those belonging to the Five Marchmounts.
translations.idiomatic: Those facing outward from the inner ring represented the Five Planets, the stellar gods of the central palace and the five bureaus, and the marchmounts and their affiliates.

sentences.zh: 背外營神，二十八宿外官星，雷公、先農、風伯、雨師、四海、四瀆、名山、大川之屬也。

translations.literal: The spirits with their backs to the outer enclosure are the Twenty-Eight Lodges’ outer star officials, Thunder Duke, First Farmer, Wind Earl, Rain Master, the Four Seas, the Four Great Rivers, famous mountains, great rivers, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: The outer ring’s outward-facing gods included the Twenty-Eight Mansions and outer asterisms, Thunder Duke, the god of agriculture, Wind and Rain, the four seas and four channel rivers, and celebrated peaks and streams.

sentences.zh: 至七年五月，詔三公曰：「漢當郊尧。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year, he issued an edict to the Three Excellencies, saying, “Han ought to sacrifice to Yao at the suburbs.”
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Jianwu 7 (31 CE), he told the Three Excellencies that the dynasty should institute suburban rites in honor of the sage-king Yao.

sentences.zh: 其与卿大夫、博士议。

translations.literal: Let them deliberate together with ministers, great officers, and erudits.
translations.idiomatic: He bade them take counsel with senior ministers and academicians.

sentences.zh: 」時侍御史杜林上疏，以爲「漢起不因缘尧，与殷、周異宜，而舊制以高帝配。

translations.literal: ” At that time Attendant Censor Du Lin presented a memorial, holding that “Han’s rise did not follow a line from Yao; its proper observances differ from those of Yin and Zhou, whereas the old arrangement matches Emperor Gao.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Attendant Censor Du Lin soon submitted a memorial arguing that the Han had not derived its legitimacy from Yao and that its ritual needs differed from Yin and Zhou practice, while the standing rule already paired the suburban altar with Emperor Gao.

sentences.zh: 方軍師在外，且可如元年郊祀故事」。

translations.literal: Since the army and its commanders are still abroad, for the moment one may follow the suburban-sacrifice precedent of the first year.”
translations.idiomatic: With the armies still in the field, he argued, the court should for now adhere to the suburban rites observed in the first year of the reign.”

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The Sovereign followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 語在《林传》。

translations.literal: The account is in the “Biography of Lin.”
translations.idiomatic: Du Lin’s memorial is preserved in his biography.

sentences.zh: 陇、蜀平后，乃增广郊祀，高帝配食，位在中壇上，西面北上。

translations.literal: After Long and Shu were pacified, then they enlarged the suburban sacrifices; Gaodi shared in the offerings, his position on the central mound, facing west, with precedence to the north.
translations.idiomatic: Once Long and Shu had been subdued, the court expanded the suburban cult and set Emperor Gao as correlative recipient on the central terrace, facing west with senior rank to the north.

sentences.zh: 天、地、高帝、黄帝各用犢一头，青帝、赤帝共用犢一头，白帝、黑帝共用犢一头，凡用犢六头。

translations.literal: Heaven, Earth, Gaodi, and the Yellow Thearch each used one calf; the Green Thearch and Red Thearch shared one calf; the White Thearch and Black Thearch shared one calf; in all six calves were used.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven, Earth, Emperor Gao, and the Yellow Thearch each received a calf; the Green and Red Thearchs shared one, as did the White and Black Thearchs—six calves in all.

sentences.zh: 日、月、北斗共用牛一头，四營羣神共用牛四头，凡用牛五头。

translations.literal: Sun, Moon, and Northern Dipper shared one ox; the four camps’ host of spirits shared four oxen; in all five oxen were used.
translations.idiomatic: The Sun, Moon, and Northern Dipper shared a single ox; the deities of the four precincts shared four more—five oxen altogether.

sentences.zh: 凡乐奏《青陽》、《朱明》、《西皓》、《玄冥》，及《云翘》、《育命》舞。

translations.literal: For music they performed “Green Yang,” “Red Brightness,” “Western Radiance,” and “Dark Obscurity,” and the dances “Cloud Crest” and “Nurturing the Mandate.”
translations.idiomatic: The musicians played the seasonal hymns *Qingyang*, *Zhuming*, *Xihao*, and *Xuanming*, accompanied by the *Yunqiao* and *Yuming* dances.

sentences.zh: 中營四門，門用席十八枚，外營四門，門用席三十六枚，凡用席二百一十六枚，皆莞簟，率一席三神。

translations.literal: The inner enclosure’s four gates, each gate used eighteen mats; the outer enclosure’s four gates, each gate used thirty-six mats; in all two hundred sixteen mats were used, all rush and bamboo mats; on average one mat for three spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Each inner gate held eighteen rush mats and each outer gate thirty-six—two hundred sixteen mats of coiled rush and bamboo, generally three deities to a mat.

sentences.zh: 日、月、北斗無陛郭醊。

translations.literal: Sun, Moon, and Northern Dipper had no stairway-enclosure zhui.
translations.idiomatic: No stepped mounds (*zhui*) ringed the stations of the Sun, Moon, or Northern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 既送神，燎俎實于壇南巳地。

translations.literal: After sending off the spirits, they burned the stand’s meat offerings on the mound’s south in the si position.
translations.idiomatic: Once the spirits had been dismissed, the meat from the sacrificial stands was burned at the south side of the altar in the si quarter.

sentences.zh: 三十二年正月，上齋，夜讀《河圖會昌符》曰：「赤劉之九，會命岱宗。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirty-second year, the Sovereign fasted; at night he read the *Hetu Huichang fu*, which said, “The ninth of the Red Liu will convene the mandate on Dai’s Marchmount.”
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jianwu 32 (56 CE), while observing the fast, he read by lamplight the *River Chart’s Talisman of Flourishing Accord*: “The ninth generation of the Red Liu will receive its charge on the Eastern Marchmount.”

sentences.zh: 不慎克用，何益于承！

translations.literal: If one does not carefully be able to use it, what benefit is there to receiving!
translations.idiomatic: Unless it is applied with scrupulous care, what good can it do the heir who receives the mandate?

sentences.zh: 誠善用之，奸伪不萌。

translations.literal: If truly one uses it well, treachery and falsehood will not sprout.
translations.idiomatic: Wielded in good faith, it leaves no room for deceit.

sentences.zh: 」感此文，乃詔松等复案索《河》、《雒》讖文言九世封禅事者。

translations.literal: ” Moved by this text, he then ordered Song and others again to search through River and Luo prophecy texts that spoke of the ninth generation’s feng and shan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: ” Stirred by these lines, he instructed Liang Song and his colleagues to comb the Yellow River and Luo River apocrypha for passages on the ninth-generation feng and shan.

sentences.zh: 松等列奏，乃許焉。

translations.literal: Song and others arrayed a memorial; then he granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Song and the others laid their findings before the throne, and the emperor gave his assent.

sentences.zh: 初，孝武帝欲求神仙，以扶方者言黄帝由封禅而後仙，于是欲封禅。

translations.literal: At first, Emperor Xiaowu desired to seek transcendents; because those who supported the methods said the Yellow Thearch through feng and shan afterward became a transcendent, therefore he desired feng and shan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Wu had sought immortality; his fangshi advisers claimed the Yellow Thearch had ascended only after performing the feng and shan rites on Mount Tai, which fired the emperor’s own ambition to do the same.

sentences.zh: 封禅不常，時人莫知。

translations.literal: Feng and shan were not constant; people of the time did not know.
translations.idiomatic: The feng and shan observances were rare, and contemporaries knew little about them.

sentences.zh: 元封元年，上以方士言作封禅器，以示羣儒，多言不合古，于是罷諸儒不用。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfeng, the Sovereign on the fangshi’s words made feng and shan vessels, to show the host of ru; many spoke that they did not match antiquity; therefore he dismissed the host of ru and did not use them.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfeng 1 (110 BCE), following his occult advisers’ advice, he had ritual gear for the feng and shan fabricated and shown to the Confucian scholars; most pronounced it uncanonical, so he set the literati aside.

sentences.zh: 三月，上東上泰山，乃上石立之泰山颠。

translations.literal: In the third month, the Sovereign went east and ascended Mount Tai; then he ascended a stone and set it up on Mount Tai’s summit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he climbed Mount Tai from the east and set a stone marker on its peak.

sentences.zh: 遂東巡海上，求仙人，無所見而還。

translations.literal: Then he toured east on the sea, seeking transcendents; seeing nothing he returned.
translations.idiomatic: He then cruised the eastern sea in search of immortals, found none, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 四月，封泰山。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, he feng’d Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he performed the feng sacrifice on Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 恐所施用非是，乃秘其事。

translations.literal: Fearing that what was employed and applied was not correct, he then concealed the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Doubting whether the procedure had been correct, he kept the details secret.

sentences.zh: 語在《漢書·郊祀志》。

translations.literal: The account is in the “Treatise on Suburban Sacrifice” in the Hanshu.
translations.idiomatic: The full story appears in the Book of Han’s “Treatise on Suburban Sacrifices.”

sentences.zh: 上許梁松等奏，乃求元封時封禅故事，议封禅所施用。

translations.literal: The Sovereign granted Liang Song and others’ memorial; then he sought the Yuanfeng-era feng and shan precedents and deliberated what feng and shan should employ and apply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the memorial from Liang Song and his colleagues, ordered a search for Western Han precedents from the Yuanfeng performance, and convened discussion of the equipment and ritual program.

sentences.zh: 有司奏當用方石再累置壇中，皆方方尺，厚一尺，用玉牒書藏方石。

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized that one ought to use square stones piled in layers placed in the mound; all were square one chi to a side, one chi thick; with a jade slip document written and stored in the square stone.
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported that the altar should hold stacked square stones a foot thick on each face, with the jade proclamation sealed inside.

sentences.zh: 牒厚五寸，长尺三寸，广五寸，有玉檢。

translations.literal: The slip was five cun thick, one chi three cun long, five cun wide, and had a jade cover-plate.
translations.idiomatic: The jade slip was five cun thick, thirteen cun long, five cun wide, and fitted with a jade sealing plate.

sentences.zh: 又用石檢十枚，列于石傍，東西各三，南北各二，皆长三尺，广一尺，厚七寸。

translations.literal: Also they used ten stone cover-plates, arrayed beside the stone; east and west three each, south and north two each; all were three chi long, one chi wide, seven cun thick.
translations.idiomatic: Ten stone sealing blocks were to flank the central stone—three on the east and west, two on the north and south—each three feet long, a foot wide, and seven inches thick.

sentences.zh: 檢中刻三處，深四寸，方五寸，有蓋。

translations.literal: In the cover-plate were carved three places, four cun deep, five cun square; there was a lid.
translations.idiomatic: Each stone seal was carved with three recesses, four inches deep and five inches square, and capped with a lid.

sentences.zh: 檢用金縷五周，以水銀和金以爲泥。

translations.literal: The cover-plate used gold thread five circuits; with mercury mixed with gold they made mud.
translations.idiomatic: They bound the seals with five turns of gold wire and sealed the joints with an amalgam of mercury and gold.

sentences.zh: 玉璽一方寸二分，一枚方五寸。

translations.literal: The jade seal was one cun two fen square; one piece was five cun square.
translations.idiomatic: One jade seal measured an inch and two tenths square; another slab measured five inches square.

sentences.zh: 方石四角又有距石，皆再累。

translations.literal: At the square stone’s four corners there were again footing stones; all were again layered.
translations.idiomatic: Corner posts were set at each angle of the central block, each built up in courses.

sentences.zh: 枚长一丈，厚一尺，广二尺，皆在圓壇上。

translations.literal: Each was one zhang long, one chi thick, two chi wide; all were on the round mound.
translations.idiomatic: Each measured ten feet in length, a foot thick, and two feet wide, standing on the round terrace.

sentences.zh: 其下用距石十八枚，皆高三尺，厚一尺，广二尺，如小碑，环壇立之，去壇三步。

translations.literal: Below it used eighteen footing stones; all were three chi high, one chi thick, two chi wide, like small steles; they ringed the mound and stood them, three paces from the mound.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen supporting stones, each three feet high and shaped like miniature steles, ringed the altar three paces out.

sentences.zh: 距石下皆有石跗，入地四尺。

translations.literal: Beneath the footing stones all had stone bases, entering the ground four chi.
translations.idiomatic: Each footing stone sat on a socket sunk four feet into the earth.

sentences.zh: 又用石碑，高九尺，广三尺五寸，厚尺二寸，立壇丙地，去壇三丈以上，以刻書。

translations.literal: Also they used a stone stele, nine chi high, three chi five cun wide, one chi two cun thick, set up on the mound’s bing ground, more than three zhang from the mound, to carve writing.
translations.idiomatic: A stone stele nine feet high, three feet five inches wide, and a little over a foot thick was raised in the bing sector more than thirty feet from the mound to bear the inscription.

sentences.zh: 上以用石功难，又欲及二月封，故詔松欲因故封石空檢，更加封而已。

translations.literal: The Sovereign, because using stone work was difficult, and also desiring to catch the second month’s feng, therefore ordered Song to desire to follow the old feng stone’s empty cover-plate and merely add sealing.
translations.idiomatic: Because quarrying new stone would be slow and he hoped to perform the feng in the second month, he initially told Liang Song to reuse the old Western Han block, hollow out a new cavity in its seal, and simply reseal it.

sentences.zh: 松上疏争之，以爲「登封之禮，告功皇天，垂后無窮，以爲萬民也。

translations.literal: Song presented a memorial disputing it, holding that “The rite of ascending to feng announces merit to August Heaven, hangs down to later ages without end, and is for the sake of the myriad people.”
translations.idiomatic: Liang Song protested in a memorial: “The feng rite proclaims your achievement to Heaven and must stand for ages to come on behalf of the people.”

sentences.zh: 承天之敬，尤宜章明。

translations.literal: Receiving Heaven’s reverence, especially ought to be made clear and bright.
translations.idiomatic: The reverence owed to Heaven ought above all to be displayed openly.

sentences.zh: 奉圖書之瑞，尤宜顯著。

translations.literal: Presenting the charts’ and documents’ auspicious signs, especially ought to be made manifest and prominent.
translations.idiomatic: The auspicious charts that justify the rite should be honored with equal clarity.

sentences.zh: 今因舊封，窜寄玉牒故石下，恐非重命之義。

translations.literal: Now relying on the old feng, furtively lodging the jade slip document under the old stone, I fear this is not the meaning of a renewed charge.
translations.idiomatic: To tuck the new jade text under the old Western Han stone would look furtive and ill suit a renewed mandate.”

sentences.zh: 受命中興，宜當特異，以明天意」。

translations.literal: Receiving the charge and restoring the dynasty, ought appropriately to be specially distinctive, to make clear Heaven’s intent.”
translations.idiomatic: This restoration deserves its own monument, plainly declaring Heaven’s will.”

sentences.zh: 遂使泰山郡及鲁趣石工，宜取完青石，無必五色。

translations.literal: Therefore he ordered Taishan commandery and Lu to hurry stoneworkers; they should take intact greenish stone; there was no necessity for five colors.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore instructed Taishan and Lu to press masons into service and quarry sound bluestone without insisting on polychrome marble.

sentences.zh: 時以印工不能刻玉牒，欲用丹漆書之；

translations.literal: At the time because seal craftsmen could not carve the jade slip document, they desired to use cinnabar lacquer to write it;
translations.idiomatic: Seal-cutters at first could not incise the jade slip, so the court considered writing the text in vermilion lacquer instead;

sentences.zh: 會求得能刻玉者，遂書。

translations.literal: In the end they sought and obtained one able to carve jade; then they wrote it.
translations.idiomatic: but when a craftsman skilled in jade carving was found, the text was engraved after all.

sentences.zh: 書秘刻方石中，命容玉牒。

translations.literal: The writing was secretly carved inside the square stone, ordered to contain the jade slip document.
translations.idiomatic: The inscription was cut secretly into the square stone, hollowed to receive the jade document.

sentences.zh: 二月，上至奉高，遣侍御史与蘭臺令史，將工先上山刻石。

translations.literal: In the second month, the Sovereign arrived at Fenggao; he dispatched an attendant censor and a Lan-tai clerk of records, leading workmen first up the mountain to carve the stone.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the emperor reached Fenggao and sent an attendant censor and a palace clerk to lead workmen up the mountain ahead of him to cut the stele.

sentences.zh: 文曰：

translations.literal: The text said:
translations.idiomatic: The inscription read:

sentences.zh: 二十五日甲午，禅，祭地于梁阴，以高后配，山川羣神從，如元始中北郊故事。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth day, jiawu, they performed the shan; they sacrificed to Earth on Liang’s shady side, with Empress Gao as correlative; mountains and rivers and the host of spirits followed, according to the Yuanshi-era northern suburban precedent.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth day, a jiawu day, he performed the shan, offering to Earth on the northern slope of Mount Liang with Empress Lü as consort and the terrestrial spirits in attendance, following the northern-suburban model of the Yuanshi era.

sentences.zh: 四月己卯，大赦天下，以建武三十二年爲建武中元元年，复博、奉高、赢勿出元年租、刍稿。

translations.literal: On jimao of the fourth month, he greatly pardoned all under Heaven; he took Jianwu thirty-second year as Jianwu middle era first year; he restored Bo, Fenggao, and Ying so as not to issue the first year’s rent and straw.
translations.idiomatic: On the jimao day of the fourth month he proclaimed a general amnesty, renamed the year from Jianwu 32 to the first year of the Zhongyuan era, and remitted rent and fodder levies for Bo, Fenggao, and Ying for that year.

sentences.zh: 以吉日刻玉牒書函藏金匮，璽印封之。

translations.literal: On an auspicious day they carved the jade slip document’s case and stored it in a metal coffer; with seal impressions they sealed it.
translations.idiomatic: On an auspicious day the jade text was boxed, placed in a metal casket, and sealed with the imperial seals.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，使太尉行事，以特告至高廟。

translations.literal: On yiyou, he ordered the Grand Commandant to conduct the affair, with a bull specially [raised] to announce to Gaodi’s temple.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou he had the Grand Commandant officiate and announce the deed at Gaodi’s temple with a specially prepared bull.

sentences.zh: 太尉奉匮以告高廟，藏于廟室西壁石室高主室之下。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant bore the coffer to announce to Gaodi’s temple; it was stored beneath Gaodi’s chamber in the temple room’s west wall stone chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant presented the coffer at the shrine to Emperor Gao and deposited it in the stone vault under the western wall of the inner sanctum.
